title: Experimental Analysis of Detector Noise in Scanning Electron Microscopy
content: Noise in scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is one of the most fundamental limiting factors for lose-dose high-resolution imaging. There are various noise models, denoising techniques, event-counting based imaging schemes with the aim to improve signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the images produced in an SEM [1-4]. In widely accepted practice in the community, the focus on improving the result has been prioritized while sacrificing rigorous characterization of the behavior of the individual sub-parts.
